value.zh: 月五星犯列舍經星變附見
value.en: The Moon and the Five Planets Transgressing the Lodges and Classical Stars, with Supplementary Notes on Celestial Portents.
value.literal: Transgressions of the Moon and the Five Planets against the Lodges and Classical Stars; appended observations on anomalies.

value.zh: 少帝正始元年四月戊午，月犯昴東頭第一星。
value.en: On wuwu in the fourth month of Zhengshi 1 of the Young Emperor the moon clipped the easternmost star of the Hairy Head.
value.literal: On wuwu in the fourth month of Zhengshi 1 of the Young Emperor the Moon transgressed the first star at the eastern end of the Hairy Head [Pleiades region].

value.zh: 十月庚寅，月又犯昴北斗四星。
value.en: On gengyin in the tenth month the moon transited both the Hairy Head and four stars of the Northern Dipper.
value.literal: On gengyin in the tenth month the Moon again transgressed the Hairy Head and the four stars of the Northern Dipper.

value.zh: 占曰：「月犯昴，胡不安。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "When the moon trespasses against Mao, the Hu will be unsettled."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “When the Moon transgresses the Hairy Head, the Hu are restless.

value.zh: 二年六月，鮮卑阿妙兒等寇西方，敦煌太守王延破之，斬二萬餘級。
value.en: In the second year’s sixth month Xianbei bands led by Amiao’er struck the western marches; Dunhuang prefect Wang Yan routed them, claiming over twenty thousand heads.
value.literal: In the sixth month of the second year Xianbei under Amiao’er and others raided the west; prefect Wang Yan of Dunhuang defeated them and beheaded more than twenty thousand.

value.zh: 三年，又斬鮮卑大師及千餘級。
value.en: The third year saw another victory that took the Xianbei commander’s head plus more than a thousand others.
value.literal: In the third year another campaign severed the Xianbei commander’s head and over a thousand others.

value.zh: 二年九月癸酉，月犯輿鬼西北星。
value.en: On guiyou in the second year’s ninth month the moon crossed the Ghosts’ northwest star.
value.literal: On guiyou in the ninth month of the second year the Moon transgressed the northwest star of the Ghosts.

value.zh: 三年二月丁未，又犯西南星。
value.en: On dingwei in the third year’s second month it struck the Ghosts’ southwest star.
value.literal: On dingwei in the third year’s second month it again transgressed the southwest star.

value.zh: 占曰：「有錢令。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "There will be a money ordinance."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “There will be an ordinance on coinage.

value.zh: 一曰：「大臣憂。」
value.en: A variant gloss adds: “High ministers face peril.”
value.literal: Another saying: “Great ministers will suffer.

value.zh: 三年三月，太尉滿寵薨。
value.en: Grand Commandant Man Chong died in the third month of the third year.
value.literal: In the third month of the third year Grand Commandant Man Chong died.

value.zh: 四年正月，帝加元服，賜群臣錢各有差。
value.en: The fourth year’s first month saw the emperor’s capping ceremony and graded cash gifts to his officials.
value.literal: In the first month of the fourth year the emperor assumed the capping [adult rite] and bestowed cash on the various ministers in graded amounts.

value.zh: 四年十月、十一月，月再犯井鉞。
value.en: During the fourth year’s tenth and eleventh months the moon crossed the Well’s axe twice.
value.literal: In the tenth and eleventh months of the fourth year the Moon twice transgressed the Well’s Battle-Axe.

value.zh: 是月，宣帝討諸葛恪，恪棄城走。
value.en: That month Xuandi attacked Zhuge Ke, who deserted his walls and ran.
value.literal: That same month Xuandi campaigned against Zhuge Ke, who abandoned the city and fled.

value.zh: 五年二月，曹爽征蜀。
value.en: Cao Shuang led a Shu expedition in the fifth year’s second month.
value.literal: In the second month of the fifth year Cao Shuang campaigned against Shu.

value.zh: 五年十一月癸巳，填星犯亢距星。
value.en: On guisi in the fifth year’s eleventh month Saturn crossed the Neck’s separator stars.
value.literal: On guisi in the eleventh month of the fifth year the Station Star transgressed the separator stars of the Neck [lodge].

value.zh: 占曰：「諸侯有失國者。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "Among the feudal lords there will be one who loses his state."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “Among the feudal lords there will be one who loses his state.

value.zh: 七年七月丁丑，月犯左角。
value.en: On dingchou in the seventh year’s seventh month the moon crossed the Horn’s left horn-star.
value.literal: On dingchou in the seventh month of the seventh year the Moon transgressed the left horn [of the Horn lodge].

value.zh: 占曰：「天下有兵，左將軍死。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "There will be war under Heaven, and the Left General will die."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “Under Heaven there will be soldiers; the general of the left will die.

value.zh: 七月乙亥，熒惑犯畢距星。
value.en: On yihai in the seventh month Mars crossed the Net’s separator star.
value.literal: On yihai in the seventh month Spark-Delight transgressed the separator star of the Net.

value.zh: 占曰；
value.en: The prognostication reads:
value.literal: The omen-text says:

value.zh: 「有邊兵。」
value.en: "There will be frontier troops."
value.literal: There will be troops on the frontier.

value.zh: 一曰：「刑罰用。」
value.en: One reading said, "Punishments will be used."
value.literal: Another saying: “Punishments will be applied.

value.zh: 九年正月辛亥，月犯亢南星。
value.en: On xinhai in the ninth year’s first month the moon crossed the Neck’s southern star.
value.literal: On xinhai in the first month of the ninth year the Moon transgressed the southern star of the Neck.

value.zh: 占曰：「兵起。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "War will arise."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “Arms will arise.

value.zh: 一曰：「將軍死。」
value.en: One reading said, "The general will die."
value.literal: Another saying: “A general will die.

value.zh: 七月癸丑，填星犯楗閉。
value.en: On guichou in the seventh month Saturn crossed Key-and-Bolt.
value.literal: On guichou in the seventh month the Station Star transgressed Key-and-Bolt.

value.zh: 占曰：「王者不宜出宮下殿。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "The king should not leave the palace or descend from the hall."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “The king should not leave the palace or descend the hall.

value.zh: 嘉平元年，天子謁陵，宣帝奏誅曹爽等。
value.en: Jiaping 1 saw the emperor tend the tombs while Xuandi procured orders to purge Cao Shuang’s faction.
value.literal: In the first Jiaping year the Son of Heaven visited the imperial tombs; Xuandi memorialized to execute Cao Shuang and his party.

value.zh: 天子野宿，於是失勢。
value.en: Forced to camp outside the capital, the emperor forfeited real power.
value.literal: The Son of Heaven lodged in the field encampment; thereby he lost authority.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 太子性剛，知賈謐恃後之貴，不能假借之。
value.en: Yu refused to flatter Jia Mi.
value.literal: The crown prince's temper was stiff; knowing Jia Mi relied on the empress's power, he would not indulge him.

value.zh: 謐至東宮，或舍之而於後庭遊戲。
value.en: He left Jia Mi cooling heels while he played inside.
value.literal: When Mi came to the Eastern Palace he sometimes left him waiting while he played in the inner courts.

value.zh: 詹事裴權諫曰：「賈謐甚有寵于中宮，而有不順之色，若一旦交構，大事去矣。
value.en: Household Superintendent Pei Quan remonstrated: "Jia Mi is deeply favored in the inner palace yet shows disrespectful looks—if they ever turn on you, the great enterprise is lost.
value.literal: Household Superintendent Pei Quan remonstrated: 'Jia Mi is deeply favored in the inner palace yet shows disrespectful looks—if they ever turn on you, the great enterprise is lost.

value.zh: 宜深自謙屈，以防其變，廣延賢士，用自輔翼。」
value.en: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings."
value.literal: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings.'

value.zh: 太子不能從。
value.en: Yu ignored him.
value.literal: The crown prince would not follow.

value.zh: 初，賈后母郭槐欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固。
value.en: Guo Huai once pushed a Han match—Yu wanted it too.
value.literal: Earlier Empress Jia's mother Guo Huai had wished to take Han Shou's daughter as crown princess; the crown prince also wished to marry the Hans to strengthen himself.

value.zh: 而壽妻賈午及後皆不聽，而為太子聘王衍小女惠風。
value.en: Jia Wu and the empress forced Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng instead.
value.literal: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.

value.zh: 太子聞衍長女美，而賈后為謐聘之，心不能平，頗以為言。
value.en: Yu resented losing Wang's elder beauty to Jia Mi.
value.literal: The crown prince heard Wang's elder daughter was beautiful while the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; his heart could not rest easy and he spoke of it often.

value.zh: 謐嘗與太子圍棋，爭道，成都王穎見而訶謐，謐意愈不平，因此譖太子于後曰：「太子廣買田業，多畜私財以結小人者，為賈氏故也。
value.en: Once while playing go with the crown prince Mi quarreled over a move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and slandered the crown prince to the empress: "The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.
value.literal: Once Mi played go with the crown prince and they quarreled over the move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and therefore slandered the crown prince to the empress: 'The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.

value.zh: 密聞其言云：'皇后萬歲後，吾當魚肉之。
value.en: Mi quoted Yu vowing to slaughter the Jias after Jia died.
value.literal: I have secretly heard him say: "After the empress dies, I shall butcher them."

value.zh: '非但如是也，若宮車晏駕，彼居大位，依楊氏故事，誅臣等而廢後於金墉，如反手耳。
value.en: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.
value.literal: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.

value.zh: 不如早為之所，更立慈順者以自防衛。」
value.en: Better strike early, remove him, and set up someone kindly and tractable to defend ourselves."
value.literal: Better strike early, remove him, and set up someone kindly and tractable to defend ourselves.'

value.zh: 後納其言，又宣揚太子之短，布諸遠近。
value.en: Jia adopted the plot and smeared Yu empire-wide.
value.literal: The empress accepted his words and further broadcast the crown prince's faults throughout near and far.

value.zh: 于時朝野咸知賈后有害太子意。
value.en: Everyone saw Jia meant to kill the heir.
value.literal: Then court and countryside knew the empress meant to harm the crown prince.

value.zh: 中護軍趙俊請太子廢後，太子不聽。
value.en: Zhao Jun urged preemptive deposition—Yu declined.
value.literal: Central Guard Zhao Jun asked the crown prince to depose the empress first; the crown prince refused.

value.zh: 初，太子之廢也，妃父王衍表請離婚。
value.en: Wang Yan filed for divorce the moment Yu fell.
value.literal: When the crown prince was first deposed, his father-in-law Wang Yan memorialized requesting divorce.

value.zh: 太子至許，遺妃書曰：「鄙雖頑愚，心念為善，欲盡忠孝之節，無有惡逆之心。
value.en: After reaching Xu he sent his consort a letter: "Though I am coarse and foolish, at heart I wished to do good and fulfill loyalty and filial piety—I harbored no rebellious evil.
value.literal: After the crown prince reached Xu he sent his consort a letter: 'Though I am coarse and foolish at heart I wished to do good and fulfill loyalty and filial piety—I harbored no rebellious evil.

value.zh: 雖非中宮所生，奉事有如親母。
value.en: He claimed dutiful service to Jia despite birth.
value.literal: Though not born of the inner palace I served her as my own mother.

value.zh: 自為太子以來，敕見禁檢，不得見母。
value.en: Palace rules barred him from Lady Xie.
value.literal: Since becoming crown prince edicts confined me—I could not see my mother.

value.zh: 自宜城君亡，不見存恤，恆在空室中坐。
value.en: Since the Lady of Yicheng died I received no comforting word—I constantly sat alone in empty rooms.
value.literal: Since the Lady of Yicheng died I received no comforting word—I constantly sat alone in empty rooms.

value.zh: 去年十二月，道文疾病困篤，父子之情，實相憐湣。
value.en: Last twelfth month Daowen became gravely ill; the affection between father and son made us deeply pity one another.
value.literal: Last twelfth month Daowen's illness grew desperate—father and son pitied each other truly.

value.zh: 于時表國家乞加徽號，不見聽許。
value.en: His plea for son's title failed.
value.literal: Then I petitioned the throne for honors—permission never came.

value.zh: 疾病既篤，為之求請恩福，無有噁心。
value.en: He denied malice in praying for the boy.
value.literal: When illness grew grave I sought blessings for him—I bore no evil intent.

value.zh: 自道文病，中宮三遣左右來視，云：'天教呼汝。
value.en: Since Daowen fell ill, the empress sent attendants three times to see me, saying, "His Majesty summons you."
value.literal: Since Daowen fell ill, the empress sent attendants three times to see me, saying, "His Majesty summons you."

value.zh: '到二十八日暮，有短函來，題言東宮發，疏云：'言天教欲見汝。
value.en: On the evening of the twenty-eighth a short letter arrived, marked as a dispatch from the Eastern Palace. It said, "His Majesty wishes to see you."
value.literal: On the evening of the twenty-eighth a short letter arrived, marked as a dispatch from the Eastern Palace. It said, "His Majesty wishes to see you."

value.zh: '即便作表求入。
value.en: He requested audience.
value.literal: At once I drafted a memorial begging entry.

value.zh: 二十九日早入見國家，須臾遣至中宮。
value.en: He saw Hui briefly then reached Jia's halls.
value.literal: On the twenty-ninth morning I entered and saw His Majesty; presently I was sent to the inner palace.

value.zh: 中宮左右陳舞見語：'中宮旦來吐不快。
value.en: Chen Wu claimed Jia was sick.
value.literal: Inner attendants Chen Wu told him: 'The empress vomited ill this morning.'

value.zh: '使住空屋中坐。
value.en: They parked him in an empty room.
value.literal: She told you to wait seated in an empty chamber.

value.zh: 須臾中宮遣陳舞見語：'聞汝表陛下為道文乞王，不得王是成國耳。
value.en: Presently the empress sent Chen Wu to tell me: 'I hear you petitioned His Majesty to make Daowen a prince and were refused. A princely title means a territorial domain, after all.'
value.literal: Presently the empress sent Chen Wu to tell me: 'I hear you petitioned His Majesty to make Daowen a prince and were refused. A princely title means a territorial domain, after all.'

value.zh: '中宮遙呼陳舞：'昨天教與太子酒棗。
value.en: The empress called to Chen Wu from a distance: "Yesterday His Majesty ordered wine and jujubes for the crown prince."
value.literal: The empress called to Chen Wu from a distance: "Yesterday His Majesty ordered wine and jujubes for the crown prince."

value.zh: '便持三升酒、大盤棗來見與，使飲酒啖棗盡。
value.en: Chen Wu forced three sheng wine and dates.
value.literal: She brought three sheng of ale and a great tray of jujubes and made him finish both.

value.zh: 鄙素不飲酒，即便遣舞啟說不堪三升之意。
value.en: Yu pleaded low tolerance.
value.literal: I never drink ale yet sent Chen Wu back explaining I could not manage three sheng.

value.zh: 中宮遙呼曰：'汝常陛下前持酒可喜，何以不飲？
value.en: The empress called from a distance: 'You are always so pleasing when you hold wine before His Majesty; why will you not drink?'
value.literal: The empress called from a distance: 'You are always so pleasing when you hold wine before His Majesty; why will you not drink?'

value.zh: 天與汝酒，當使道文差也。
value.en: His Majesty has given you wine; it should make Daowen recover.
value.literal: His Majesty has given you wine; it should make Daowen recover.

value.zh: '便答中宮：'陛下會同一日見賜，故不敢辭，通日不飲三升酒也。
value.en: Yu cited earlier imperial banquet.
value.literal: I answered the inner palace: His Majesty granted ale one day—therefore I dared not refuse—but all day I never drank three sheng.

value.zh: 且實未食，恐不堪。
value.en: Empty stomach worried him.
value.literal: Moreover I had not eaten—I feared I could not endure it.

value.zh: 又未見殿下，飲此或至顛倒。
value.en: Besides, I had not yet seen Your Highness, and drinking this might leave me confused and unsteady.
value.literal: Nor had I yet seen Your Highness—I feared drink might overturn me.

value.zh: '陳舞復傳語云：'不孝那！
value.en: Chen Wu called him unfilial.
value.literal: Chen Wu relayed another message: "You unfilial wretch!

value.zh: 天與汝酒飲，不肯飲，中有惡物邪？
value.en: His Majesty gives you wine to drink, yet you refuse. Is there something harmful in it?
value.literal: His Majesty gives you wine to drink, yet you refuse. Is there something harmful in it?

value.zh: '遂可飲二升，餘有一升，求持還東宮飲盡。
value.en: I then managed to drink two sheng. With one sheng left, I asked to take it back to the Eastern Palace and finish it there.
value.literal: I then managed to drink two sheng. With one sheng left, I asked to take it back to the Eastern Palace and finish it there.

value.zh: 逼迫不得已，更飲一升。
value.en: Cornered he drank more.
value.literal: Pressed helplessly he drank another sheng.

value.zh: 飲已，體中荒迷，不復自覺。
value.en: After drinking it, I became dazed and lost awareness.
value.literal: After drinking his body grew confused and he lost awareness.

value.zh: 須臾有一小婢持封箱來，云：'詔使寫此文書。
value.en: Presently a young maid brought a sealed case and said, "The emperor orders you to copy this document."
value.literal: Presently a young maid brought a sealed case, saying, 'The edict orders you to write out this document.'

value.zh: '鄙便驚起，視之，有一白紙，一青紙。
value.en: He found white and green paper inside.
value.literal: I started in alarm and looked: there was one sheet of white paper and one of green.

value.zh: 催促云：'陛下停待。
value.en: Runners said the emperor waited.
value.literal: They pressed: 'His Majesty is waiting.'

value.zh: '又小婢承福持筆研墨黃紙來，使寫。
value.en: Chengfu added brush and yellow paper for the copy.
value.literal: Another small maid, Chengfu, brought brush, inkstone, and yellow paper, making him write.

value.zh: 急疾不容復視，實不覺紙上語輕重。
value.en: Rush left no time to read the forgery's sense.
value.literal: Haste would not let me reread; I truly did not notice the import of the words on the page.

value.zh: 父母至親，實不相疑，事理如此，實為見誣，想眾人見明也。」
value.en: Parents are kin closest of all—I truly did not doubt them; though matters went so, I have been slandered, and I trust the multitude will see it clear.'
value.literal: Parents are kin closest of all—I truly did not doubt them; though matters went so, I have been slandered, and I trust the multitude will see it clear.'

value.zh: 孫惠
value.en: Sun Hui.
value.literal: Section heading: Sun Hui.

value.zh: 鑒弟濤及弟子戭，並有才筆。
value.en: His brother Wang Tao and his nephew Wang Yan were both fine writers.
value.literal: Jian's younger brother Tao and his nephew Yan both had talent with the brush.

value.zh: 濤字茂略，曆著作郎、無錫令。
value.en: Wang Tao, courtesy Maolue, rose through editorial director to magistrate of Wuxi.
value.literal: Tao, courtesy name Maolue, successively served as editorial director and magistrate of Wuxi.

value.zh: 戭字庭堅，亦為著作。
value.en: Wang Yan, courtesy Tingjian, also held a compiler's post.
value.literal: Yan, courtesy name Tingjian, also served as editorial director.

value.zh: 並早卒。
value.en: Both died young.
value.literal: Both died early.

value.zh: 序
value.en: Preface
value.literal: Preface

value.zh: 曹攄，字顏遠，譙國譙人也。
value.en: Cao Shu (courtesy Yanyuan) came from Qiao in the Qiao princedom.
value.literal: Cao Shu, courtesy name Yanyuan, was a native of Qiao in the Principality of Qiao.

value.zh: 祖肇，魏衛將軍。
value.en: His grandfather Cao Zhao had been Wei General of the Guards.
value.literal: His grandfather Zhao was Wei General of the Guards.

value.zh: 攄少有孝行，好學善屬文，太尉王衍見而器之，調補臨淄令。
value.en: Filial from boyhood, bookish and eloquent, he impressed grand commandant Wang Yan, who moved him to magistrate of Linzi.
value.literal: Shu from youth showed filial conduct, loved learning and was skilled at composition; Grand Commandant Wang Yan saw him and esteemed him; he was transferred and appointed magistrate of Linzi.

value.zh: 縣有寡婦，養姑甚謹。
value.en: The county had a widow who nursed her mother-in-law devotedly.
value.literal: In the county was a widow who tended her mother-in-law very carefully.

value.zh: 姑以其年少，勸令改適，婦守節不移。
value.en: The elder, pitying her youth, urged her to remarry; the widow refused to abandon her vow.
value.literal: The mother-in-law, because she was young, urged her to remarry; the woman kept her chastity and would not move.

value.zh: 姑湣之，密自殺。
value.en: The mother-in-law, heartsick for her, committed suicide in secret.
value.literal: The mother-in-law pitied her and secretly killed herself.

value.zh: 親党告婦殺姑，官為考鞫，寡婦不勝苦楚，乃自誣。
value.en: Kin accused the widow of murder; torture broke her and she confessed to a crime she did not commit.
value.literal: Relatives reported the woman had killed her mother-in-law; officials interrogated her under torture; the widow could not endure the pain and falsely confessed.

value.zh: 獄當決，適值攄到。
value.en: Sentence was about to fall when Cao Shu took office.
value.literal: When the case was to be decided, it happened that Shu arrived.

value.zh: 攄知其有冤，更加辯究，具得情實，時稱其明。
value.en: He sensed a miscarriage, reopened the file, and extracted the truth; contemporaries praised his insight.
value.literal: Shu knew there was injustice and investigated further; he obtained the full truth of the situation; he was at the time praised for his clarity.

value.zh: 獄有死囚，歲夕，攄行獄，湣之，曰：「卿等不幸致此非所，如何？
value.en: In the jail were condemned prisoners; at year's end Shu inspected the prison and pitied them, saying: 'You have unfortunately come to this place—what can be done?
value.literal: In the jail were condemned prisoners; at year's end Shu inspected the prison and pitied them, saying: 'You have unfortunately come to this place—what can be done?

value.zh: 新歲人情所重，豈不欲暫見家邪？」
value.en: New Year's is what human feelings most treasure—do you not wish briefly to see your families?'
value.literal: New Year's is what human feelings most treasure—do you not wish briefly to see your families?'

value.zh: 眾囚皆涕泣曰：「若得暫歸，死無恨也。」
value.en: All the prisoners wept and said: 'If we could return for a little while, we would die without regret.'
value.literal: All the prisoners wept and said: 'If we could return for a little while, we would die without regret.'

value.zh: 攄悉開獄出之，克日令還。
value.en: He threw open the gates, freed them all, and named the day they must return.
value.literal: Shu opened all the prisons and released them, setting a deadline for their return.

value.zh: 掾吏固爭，咸謂不可。
value.en: His aides protested that the risk was insane.
value.literal: The clerks firmly objected, all saying it could not be done.

value.zh: 攄曰：「此雖小人，義不見負，自為諸君任之。」
value.en: Shu said: 'Though these are petty men, in honor they will not betray me; I myself answer for them to you gentlemen.'
value.literal: Shu said: 'Though these are petty men, in honor they will not betray me; I myself answer for them to you gentlemen.'

value.zh: 至日，相率而還，並無違者，一縣嘆服，號曰聖君。
value.en: Every man returned on time; the county hailed him as a sage official.
value.literal: When the day came they came back together; none broke the promise—the whole county marveled and submitted, calling him the sage lord.

value.zh: 入為尚書郎，轉洛陽令，仁惠明斷，百姓懷之。
value.en: He reached the Masters of Writing and then Luoyang county—kind, sharp, and beloved.
value.literal: He entered [court] as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, transferred to magistrate of Luoyang; benevolent, kind, and clear in judgment—the common people cherished him.

value.zh: 時天大雨雪，宮門夜失行馬，群官檢察，莫知所在。
value.en: One night of blizzard the palace gate's traveling barriers vanished; no search turned them up.
value.literal: At that time heaven sent great rain and snow; at night the traveling barriers at the palace gate were lost; the various officials searched and none knew where they were.

value.zh: 攄使收門士，眾官咸謂不然。
value.en: Cao Shu arrested the gate guards; colleagues called it nonsense.
value.literal: Shu ordered the gate guards seized; all the officials said it was wrong.

value.zh: 攄曰：「宮掖禁嚴，非外人所敢盜，必是門士以燎寒耳。」
value.en: Shu said: 'The palace is strictly forbidden—outsiders would not dare steal them; it must be the gate guards taking them to warm themselves by fire.'
value.literal: Shu said: 'The palace is strictly forbidden—outsiders would not dare steal them; it must be the gate guards taking them to warm themselves by fire.'

value.zh: 詰之，果服。
value.en: Questioning proved him right.
value.literal: When questioned, they indeed confessed.

value.zh: 以病去官。
value.en: Illness forced him out.
value.literal: He left office due to illness.

value.zh: 復為洛陽令。
value.en: Luoyang eventually recalled him.
value.literal: Again became magistrate of Luoyang.

value.zh: 苻丕 苻登
value.en: This chapter records Fu Pi and Fu Deng.
value.literal: Fu Pi; Fu Deng.

value.zh: 堅尚書令、魏昌公苻纂自關中來奔，拜太尉，進封東海王。
value.en: Fu Zuan, Fu Jian's director of the secretariat and duke of Weichang, arrived as a refugee from Guanzhong; Fu Pi named him grand commandant and raised him to prince of Donghai.
value.literal: Fu Jian's Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Weichang Fu Zuan came fleeing from Guanzhong and was appointed Grand Commandant, advanced to Prince of Donghai.

value.zh: 以中山太守王兗為平東將軍、平州刺史、阜城侯，苻定為征東將軍、冀州牧、高城侯，苻紹為鎮東將軍、督冀州諸軍事、重合侯，苻謨為征西將軍、幽州牧、高邑侯，苻亮為鎮北大將軍、督幽、并二州諸軍事，並進爵郡公。
value.en: Wang Yan of Zhongshan became general who pacifies the east, inspector of Pingzhou, and marquis of Fucheng; Fu Ding general who conquers the east, governor of Jizhou, and marquis of Gaocheng; Fu Shao general who guards the east, with overall command in Jizhou, and marquis of Chonghe; Fu Mo general who conquers the west, governor of Youzhou, and marquis of Gaoyi; Fu Liang general who guards the north, with joint authority over You and Bing—all were promoted to commandery dukes.
value.literal: He made the Administrator of Zhongshan Wang Yan General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Pingzhou, and Marquis of Fucheng; Fu Ding General Who Conquers the East, Governor of Jizhou, and Marquis of Gaocheng; Fu Shao General Who Guards the East, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Jizhou, and Marquis of Chonghe; Fu Mo General Who Conquers the West, Governor of Youzhou, and Marquis of Gaoyi; Fu Liang General Who Guards the North, Commander of Military Affairs in You and Bing, and all were advanced in noble rank to Dukes of commanderies.

value.zh: 定、紹據信都，謨、亮先據常山，慕容垂之圍鄴城也，並降于垂，聞丕稱尊號，遣使謝罪。
value.en: Fu Ding and Fu Shao held Xindu while Fu Mo and Fu Liang had seized Changshan first; both pairs had gone over to Murong Chui when he invested Ye, yet when Fu Pi declared himself emperor they dispatched messengers begging forgiveness.
value.literal: Ding and Shao held Xindu; Mo and Liang had first occupied Changshan; when Murong Chui besieged Ye they had both surrendered to Chui, but on hearing that Fu Pi had assumed the imperial title they sent envoys to apologize.

value.zh: 王兗固守博陵，與垂相持。
value.en: Wang Yan shut himself in Boling and held the line against Murong Chui.
value.literal: Wang Yan stubbornly defended Boling against Chui.

value.zh: 左將軍竇沖、秦州刺史王統、河州刺史毛興、益州刺史王廣、南秦州刺史楊璧、衛將軍楊定，並據隴右，遣使招丕，請討姚萇。
value.en: Dou Chong, general of the left; Wang Tong, inspector of Qinzhou; Mao Xing, inspector of Hezhou; Wang Guang, inspector of Yizhou; Yang Bi, inspector of south Qinzhou; and Yang Ding, general of the guards, each held ground in Longyou and wrote to Fu Pi offering to strike Yao Chang.
value.literal: The General of the Left Dou Chong, the Inspector of Qinzhou Wang Tong, the Inspector of Hezhou Mao Xing, the Inspector of Yizhou Wang Guang, the Inspector of South Qinzhou Yang Bi, and the General of the Guards Yang Ding all held Longyou and sent envoys to summon Fu Pi, asking to campaign against Yao Chang.

value.zh: 丕大悅，以定為驃騎大將軍、雍州牧，沖為征西大將軍、梁州牧，統鎮西大將軍，興車騎大將軍，璧征南大將軍，並開府儀同三司，加散騎常侍，廣安西將軍，皆進位州牧。
value.en: Fu Pi was delighted: Yang Ding became grand general of agile cavalry and governor of Yongzhou; Dou Chong grand general who conquers the west and governor of Liangzhou; Wang Tong grand general who guards the west; Mao Xing grand general of chariots and cavalry; Yang Bi grand general who conquers the south—each with an independent headquarters and honors matching the three dukes, plus the title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary; Wang Guang became general who pacifies the west; all were raised to governorships.
value.literal: Fu Pi was greatly pleased; he made Yang Ding Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Yongzhou, Chong Grand General Who Conquers the West and Governor of Liangzhou, Tong Grand General Who Guards the West, Xing Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Bi Grand General Who Conquers the South, all with the privilege of opening a general's office with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and the additional title of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Guang General Who Pacifies the West, all advanced to the position of provincial governor.

value.zh: 先是，慕容驎攻王兗於博陵，至是糧竭矢盡，郡功曹張猗逾城聚眾應驎。
value.en: Before this, Murong Lin had been besieging Wang Yan in Boling; supplies and arrows ran out, and Zhang Yi, the county merit clerk, scaled the walls, raised a band of followers, and opened the city to Lin.
value.literal: Earlier, Murong Lin had attacked Wang Yan at Boling; by now grain and arrows were exhausted, and the county merit officer Zhang Yi climbed the wall, gathered a crowd, and went over to Lin.

value.zh: 袞臨城數之曰：「卿，秦之人也。
value.en: Wang Yan appeared on the battlements and cried out, "You were born a subject of Qin.
value.literal: Yan stood on the wall and rebuked him, saying: "You are a man of Qin.

value.zh: 吾，卿之君也。
value.en: I am the lord you serve.
value.literal: I am your lord.

value.zh: 起眾應賊，號稱義兵，何名實相違之甚！
value.en: You rouse the people for the rebels yet name it a loyal host—never was deed and title so at odds!
value.literal: You raised a host to answer the bandit and call it a righteous army—how far name and fact are twisted!

value.zh: 卿兄往合鄉宗，親逐城主，天地不容，為世大戮。
value.en: Your brother once mustered the clan, chased the lawful governor from the walls, and earned the scorn of heaven and earth—a public enemy while he lived.
value.literal: Your elder brother once joined your village kin, personally drove out the city's master; heaven and earth would not shelter him—he became the great criminal of his age.

value.zh: 身滅未幾，卿復續之。
value.en: He has scarcely paid for his crimes in the grave, and you follow in his footsteps.
value.literal: His person was destroyed not long ago, and you have taken up his course.

value.zh: 卿見為吾吏，親尋干戈，競為戎首，為爾君者，不亦難乎！
value.en: You served under my banner, then seized weapons with your own hands and led the alien host—what lord could forgive such a thing?
value.literal: You have been my officer, yet you personally took up arms and strove to be chief among the barbarians—for your lord, is that not hard indeed!

value.zh: 今人何取卿一切之功，寧能忘卿不忠不孝之事！
value.en: Men may praise your little coup today, but they will not forget that you are faithless to your prince and heartless toward your kin!
value.literal: What do men value in your petty moment of glory—can they forget your deeds of disloyalty and unfilial impiety!

value.zh: 古人有雲，求忠臣必出孝子之門，卿母在城，不能顧之，何忠義之可望！
value.en: The old proverb runs that loyal servants come from filial homes; your mother is trapped in this town while you betray it—where is your duty or your honor?
value.literal: The ancients said, seek loyal ministers among the households of filial sons; your mother is inside the city and you do not care for her—what loyalty or righteousness can be expected!

value.zh: 惡不絕世，卿之謂也。
value.en: They say wickedness outlives a single life—you prove the saying.
value.literal: Evil does not die with the generation—this is said of you.

value.zh: 不圖中州禮義之邦邦，而卿門風若斯。
value.en: I never thought to see, in the heartland where rites and duty are taught, a family sink to such conduct as yours.
value.literal: I did not expect that in the Central Plains, the land of ritual and propriety, the conduct of your clan should be thus.

value.zh: 卿去老母如脫屣，吾復何論哉！」
value.en: You abandoned your old mother like a pair of worn-out sandals—I have nothing left to say to you!"
value.literal: You cast off your aged mother as one casts off worn shoes—what more is there for me to say!"

value.zh: 既而城陷，兗及固安侯苻鑒，並為驎所殺。
value.en: The city soon fell; Wang Yan and Fu Jian, marquis of Gu'an, were both slain by Murong Lin.
value.literal: Soon the city fell; Yan and the Marquis of Gu'an Fu Jian were both killed by Lin.

value.zh: 劉皞，字克明，晉丞相譙國公句之弟也。
value.en: Liu Hao, whose courtesy name was Keming, was the younger brother of Liu Gou, Duke of Qiao and chancellor of Jin.
value.literal: Liu Hao, courtesy name Keming, was the younger brother of Liu Gou, Duke of Qiao and chancellor of Jin.

value.zh: 句，《晉書》有傳。
value.en: Gou has a biography in the 《Book of Jin》.
value.literal: Gou has a biography in the 《Book of Jin》.

value.zh: 皞少離鄉里，唐天祐中，梁將劉鄩襲太原，軍至樂平，時皞客於縣舍，為鄩軍所俘。
value.en: Hao had left his hometown while still young. During the Tianyou reign of Tang, the Liang general Liu Xun attacked Taiyuan; when his army reached Leping, Hao was staying at the county inn and was taken prisoner by Xun's forces.
value.literal: Hao left his native place while still young. In the Tianyou era of Tang, the Liang general Liu Xun raided Taiyuan; when the army reached Leping, Hao was lodging at the county guesthouse and was captured by Xun's troops.

value.zh: 謝彥章見之，知其儒者，待之以禮，謂其鄉人劉去非曰：「為君得一宗人。」
value.en: When Xie Yanzhang saw him, he recognized a man of learning and treated him courteously. He told his fellow townsman Liu Qufei, "I have found a kinsman for you."
value.literal: Xie Yanzhang saw him, knew he was a scholar, and treated him with courtesy. He said to his fellow townsman Liu Qufei, "I have found a kinsman for you."

value.zh: 即令皞見之，去非詢其爵裏，乃親族也，對泣久之，自是隨去非客於彥章門下。
value.en: He then had Hao brought to meet him. Qufei inquired into his title and home district and found they were relatives; the two wept together for a long while. Thereafter Hao followed Qufei as a client in Yanzhang's entourage.
value.literal: He then had Hao brought before him. Qufei asked about his rank and native place and found they were kin; the two wept together for a long time. From then on Hao followed Qufei as a guest in Yanzhang's household.

value.zh: 彥章得罪，去非為郢州刺史，皞隨之郡。
value.en: After Yanzhang fell from grace, Qufei was appointed prefect of Yingzhou, and Hao went with him to the prefecture.
value.literal: When Yanzhang fell from favor, Qufei became prefect of Yingzhou, and Hao accompanied him to the prefecture.

value.zh: 莊宗平河洛，去非以嘗從劉守奇歸梁，深懼獲罪，乃棄郡投高季興於荊南，皞累為荊州攝官。
value.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified the central plains, Qufei—who had once followed Liu Shouqi in defecting to Liang—feared severe punishment. He abandoned his post and threw in his lot with Gao Jixing in southern Jing; Hao served repeatedly as acting official in Jingzhou.
value.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified the Yellow River region, Qufei, having once followed Liu Shouqi in surrendering to Liang, greatly feared punishment. He abandoned his prefecture and went to Gao Jixing in Jingnan; Hao repeatedly served as acting official in Jingzhou.

value.zh: 既而兄句明宗朝為學士，遣人召歸。
value.en: Later his elder brother Gou became a Hanlin academician under Emperor Mingzong and sent for him to return.
value.literal: Later his elder brother Gou became an academician in the court of Emperor Mingzong and sent someone to summon him home.

value.zh: 梁漢颙鎮鄧州，辟為從事，入為監察御史，歷水部員外郎、史館修撰。
value.en: Liang Hanyong, military governor of Dengzhou, took him on as an aide. He then entered the capital as investigating censor and went on to serve as vice director of the Water Ministry and compiler in the Historiography Institute.
value.literal: Liang Hanyong governed Dengzhou and recruited him as an aide; he entered the capital as investigating censor, then served as vice director of the Water Ministry and compiler in the Historiography Institute.

value.zh: 長興末，宰臣趙鳳鎮邢臺，表為節度判官。
value.en: Near the end of the Changxing era, Chief Minister Zhao Feng was posted to Xingtai and recommended him as adjutant to the military commissioner.
value.literal: At the end of the Changxing era, the chief minister Zhao Feng governed Xingtai and recommended him as military commissioner adjutant.

value.zh: 清泰初，入為起居郎，改駕部員外郎，兼侍御史知雜事，移河南少尹、兵部郎中，轉太府卿。
value.en: Early in the Qingtai era he entered court as recorder of imperial activity, then became vice director of the Transport Ministry while also serving as attendant censor in charge of miscellaneous business. He was later posted as vice director of Henan, director of the War Ministry, and finally minister of the Grand Treasury.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Qingtai era he entered service as recorder of the emperor's movements, was transferred to vice director of the Transport Ministry, and concurrently served as attendant censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs. He was moved to vice director of Henan, director of the War Ministry, and then minister of the Grand Treasury.

value.zh: 漢祖受命，用為宗正卿。
value.en: When the founder of Later Han took the throne, he was appointed director of the Imperial Clan Court.
value.literal: When the Han founder received the mandate, Hao was appointed director of the Imperial Clan Court.

value.zh: 周初，改衛尉卿。
value.en: Early in the Zhou dynasty he was made minister of the Palace Guard.
value.literal: At the beginning of Zhou he was transferred to minister of the Palace Guard.

value.zh: 王延，字世美，鄚州長豐人也。
value.en: Wang Yan, whose courtesy name was Shimei, came from Changfeng in Mozhou.
value.literal: Wang Yan, courtesy name Shimei, was a native of Changfeng in Mozhou.

value.zh: 少為儒，善詞賦，會鄉曲離亂，不獲從鄉薦，因客於浮陽，隨滄帥戴思遠入梁。
value.en: In youth he studied the classics and excelled in rhapsodies and fu; when his home region fell into chaos he could not obtain a local recommendation, so he lodged in Fuyang and followed the Cangzhou governor Dai Siyuan into Liang service.
value.literal: In youth he was a Confucian scholar, skilled in rhapsodies and fu; when his home district was torn by disorder he could not obtain local recommendation, and therefore lodged in Fuyang, following the Cangzhou governor Dai Siyuan into Liang.

value.zh: 嘗以所為賦謁梁相李琪，琪覽之，欣然曰：「此道近難其人，王生升我堂矣。」
value.en: He once presented a fu he had written to Liang Chancellor Li Qi, who read it and said with delight, "This art has lately lacked a true master—Mr. Wang has raised himself to my level."
value.literal: He once presented a fu he had written to the Liang chancellor Li Qi; Qi read it and said with pleasure, "In recent times this art has lacked its master—Mr. Wang has raised himself to my hall."

value.zh: 繇是人士稱之。
value.en: From that time men of letters spoke highly of him.
value.literal: From this men of letters praised him.

value.zh: 尋薦為即墨縣令，歷徐、宋、鄆、青四鎮從事。
value.en: He was soon recommended as magistrate of Jimo and went on to serve as aide in the Xu, Song, Yan, and Qing circuits.
value.literal: Soon he was recommended as magistrate of Jimo and successively served as aide in the four circuits of Xu, Song, Yan, and Qing.

value.zh: 長興初，鄉人馮道、趙鳳在相位，擢拜左補闕。
value.en: Early in the Changxing era his fellow townsman Feng Dao and Zhao Feng were chief ministers; he was promoted to left supplementer.
value.literal: At the beginning of Changxing his fellow townsman Feng Dao and Zhao Feng held the chief ministership; he was promoted and appointed left supplementer.

value.zh: 逾年，以水部員外知制誥遷中書舍人，賜金紫。
value.en: A year later he moved from vice director of the Water Ministry with responsibility for drafting edicts to secretariat drafter and received the gold-and-purple insignia.
value.literal: After a year he was transferred from vice director of the Water Ministry with charge of drafting edicts to secretariat drafter and was granted gold-and-purple.

value.zh: 清泰末，以本官權知貢舉。
value.en: Near the end of the Qingtai era he was appointed in his existing post to oversee the civil examinations.
value.literal: At the end of Qingtai he was appointed in his existing office to act as director of the civil examinations.

value.zh: 時有舉子崔頎者，故相協之子也。
value.en: Among the candidates was Cui Qi, son of the former chancellor Xie.
value.literal: At the time there was an examinee named Cui Qi, son of the former chancellor Xie.

value.zh: 協素與吏部尚書盧文紀不睦，及延將入貢院，文紀謂延曰：「舍人以謹重聞於時，所以去冬老夫在相位時，與諸相首以長者聞奏，用掌文衡。
value.en: Xie had long been at odds with Minister of Personnel Lu Wenji. As Yan was about to enter the examination hall, Wenji told him, "You are known for your caution and gravity; that is why last winter, when I was chief minister, I was the first among the ministers to recommend a man of mature reputation to oversee the examinations.
value.literal: Xie had long been on bad terms with the minister of Personnel Lu Wenji; as Yan was about to enter the examination compound, Wenji said to him, "You, Drafter, are known in the age for caution and weight; therefore last winter, when this old man was chief minister, I reported first among the ministers that a man of mature reputation should be appointed to hold the literary scales.

value.zh: 然貢闈取士，頗多面目。
value.en: Yet in selecting candidates for the examinations, personal connections often play a large part.
value.literal: Yet in selecting scholars in the examination compound, there are often many personal connections.

value.zh: 說者云：『越人善泅，生子方晬，乳母浮之水上。
value.en: As the saying goes: "The people of Yue are skilled swimmers; when a child is barely a month old, the wet nurse floats him on the water."
value.literal: Storytellers say: "The people of Yue are skilled at swimming; when a child is just one month old, the wet nurse floats him on the water."

value.zh: 或駭然止之，乳母曰，其父善泅，子必無溺。』
value.en: Someone alarmed tries to stop her; the wet nurse says, "His father is a skilled swimmer—the child will surely not drown."
value.literal: Someone in alarm tries to stop it; the wet nurse says, "His father is skilled at swimming—the child will surely not drown."

value.zh: 今若以名下取士，即此類也。
value.en: If you choose candidates today by family name and reputation alone, it is exactly this sort of thing.
value.literal: If today one selects scholars by name, it is just this sort of thing.

value.zh: 舍人當求實才，以副公望。」
value.en: You, as Drafter, should seek genuine talent to live up to the reputation you enjoy."
value.literal: You, Drafter, ought to seek real talent, to fulfill public expectation.

value.zh: 延退而謂人曰：「盧公之言，蓋為崔頎也。
value.en: Yan withdrew and told others, "Master Lu's remarks were surely directed at Cui Qi.
value.literal: Yan withdrew and said to others, "Master Lu's words were surely aimed at Cui Qi.

value.zh: 縱與其父不悅，致意何至此耶！」
value.en: Even if he bore ill will toward the boy's father, why make his meaning so plain!"
value.literal: Even if he was displeased with the man's father, why carry the hint to such an extent!

value.zh: 來春，以頎登甲科。
value.en: The next spring, Cui Qi placed in the highest tier of the examinations.
value.literal: The following spring, Hao passed in the top tier of the examinations.

value.zh: 其年，改御史中丞，歲滿，轉尚書右丞。
value.en: That same year he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief, and when his term ended he was transferred to Vice Director of the Right in the Ministry of State.
value.literal: That year he was made Vice Censor-in-Chief; when his term expired, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Right in the Ministry of State.

value.zh: 奉使兩浙，吳人深重之。
value.en: While serving as envoy to the Two Zhes, he won the deep respect of the people of Wu.
value.literal: On a mission to the Two Zhes, the people of Wu held him in deep esteem.

value.zh: 復命，授吏部侍郎，改尚書左丞，拜太常卿，歷工、禮、刑三尚書。
value.en: After reporting back, he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, then Vice Director of the Left in the Ministry of State, then Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, and went on to hold the ministries of Works, Rites, and Punishments in succession.
value.literal: On his return he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, then Vice Director of the Left in the Ministry of State, then Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, and served successively as Minister of Works, Rites, and Punishments.

value.zh: 以疾求分司西洛，授太子少保。
value.en: He pleaded illness and asked for a post in the Luoyang branch office in the west, and was appointed Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
value.literal: Citing illness, he requested a post in the western Luoyang branch office and was appointed Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 既而連月請告，為留臺所糾，改少傅致仕。
value.en: Before long he took medical leave month after month, was censured by the Luoyang branch office, and was reassigned as Junior Preceptor before retiring from office.
value.literal: Soon afterward he repeatedly took leave for months on end and was censured by the Luoyang branch office; he was changed to Junior Preceptor and retired.

value.zh: 廣順二年冬卒，時年七十有三。
value.en: He died in the winter of the second year of Guangshun, at the age of seventy-three.
value.literal: In the winter of the second year of Guangshun he died, aged seventy-three.

value.zh: 子億，仕皇朝為殿中丞。
value.en: His son Yi served the present dynasty as a Director in the Palace Bureau.
value.literal: His son Yi served the present dynasty as Director in the Palace Bureau.

value.zh: 南齊書卷第三 本紀第三
value.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 3, Annals 3
value.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 3, Annals 3

value.zh: 二月丙子，以左衛將軍、巴東王子響爲中護軍。
value.en: Second month, day bingzi: Xiao Zixiang, prince of Badong and general of the left guard, became central protector of the army.
value.literal: Second month, day bingzi: General of the Left Guard, Prince of Badong Xiao Zixiang, was made Central Protector of the Army.

value.zh: 己丑，詔曰：「宣尼誕敷文德，峻極自天，發輝七代，陶鈞萬品，英風獨舉，素王誰匹！
value.en: Day jichou: an edict said, "Confucius was born to spread the civil Way, lofty as heaven; seven generations felt his light, ten thousand things felt his mold; his wind stood alone—what king without a crown could equal him?
value.literal: On day jichou, an edict said: "Confucius spread civil virtue from birth, lofty to the heavens; his radiance shone through seven generations and shaped ten thousand kinds of things; his noble wind stood alone—what uncrowned king could match him!

value.zh: 功隱於當年，道深於日月。
value.en: His merit lay hidden in his lifetime; his Way runs deeper than sun and moon.
value.literal: His achievement was hidden in his own age, his Way deeper than sun and moon.

value.zh: 感麟厭世，緬邈千祀，川竭谷虛，丘夷淵塞，非但洙泗湮淪，至乃饗嘗乏主。
value.en: When the qilin came he wearied of the age and left it; a thousand years stand between us; rivers fail, valleys hollow, hills sink and depths close—not only did Zhu and Si fall silent, but even the sacrifices had no keeper.
value.literal: Sensing the qilin, he loathed the world and passed away; a thousand years stretch remote; rivers dry and valleys empty, mounds level and abysses filled—not only were the Zhu and Si lost, but even the sacrificial offerings lacked a master.

value.zh: 前王敬仰，崇脩寢廟，歲月亟流，鞠爲茂草。
value.en: Earlier kings honored him and raised his shrine; the years raced by, and it turned to wild grass.
value.literal: Former kings revered him and grandly repaired the temple; years flowed swiftly, and it became rank grass.

value.zh: 今學敩興立，實稟洪規，撫事懷人，彌增欽屬。
value.en: Now schools rise again on his great pattern; handling state, I cherish the man and my awe only grows.
value.literal: Now learning and instruction are established—truly inheriting his great rule; as I handle affairs I cherish the man all the more and my reverence deepens.

value.zh: 可改築宗祊，務在爽塏。
value.en: Rebuild the ancestral shrine on high, open ground.
value.literal: The ancestral temple may be rebuilt, striving for bright and open ground.

value.zh: 量給祭秩，禮同諸侯。
value.en: Grant sacrificial income by measure, with rites equal to a feudal lord.
value.literal: Measure out sacrificial stipends; the rites are the same as for feudal lords.

value.zh: 奉聖之爵，以時紹繼。」
value.en: Let the Fengsheng marquisate pass in due time."
value.literal: The fief of Fengsheng is to be continued in its season."

value.zh: 壬寅，以丹陽尹王晏爲江州刺史。
value.en: Day renyin: Wang Yan, intendant of Danyang, was made inspector of Jiangzhou.
value.literal: On day renyin, Palace Attendant Wang Yan was made Inspector of Jiangzhou.

value.zh: 癸卯，以巴陵王子倫爲豫州刺史。
value.en: Day guimao: Xiao Zilun, prince of Baling, took Yu.
value.literal: On day guimao, Prince of Baling Xiao Zilun was made Inspector of Yuzhou.

value.zh: 南齊書卷四十二‧列傳第二十三
value.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 42, Biographies 23
value.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 42, Biographies 23

value.zh: 王晏 蕭諶 蕭坦之 江祏
value.en: Wang Yan, Xiao Chen, Xiao Tanzhi, and Jiang Shi
value.literal: Wang Yan, Xiao Chen, Xiao Tanzhi, Jiang Shi

value.zh: 王晏字士彥，琅邪臨沂人也。
value.en: Wang Yan, courtesy name Shiyan, was a native of Linyi in Langya Commandery.
value.literal: Wang Yan, courtesy name Shiyan, was a man of Langya, Linyi.

value.zh: 祖弘之，通直常侍。
value.en: His grandfather Wang Hongzhi served as Regular Attendant of Direct Communication.
value.literal: His grandfather Hongzhi was a Regular Attendant of Direct Communication.

value.zh: 父普曜，祕書監。
value.en: His father Wang Puyao was Director of the Secretariat.
value.literal: His father Puyao was Director of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 晏，宋大明末起家臨賀王國常侍，員外郎，巴陵王征北板參軍，安成王撫軍板刑獄，隨府轉車騎。
value.en: At the end of the Liu Song Daming era, Yan began his career as a regular attendant in the princedom of Linhe, then served as an outside-section gentleman, as a staff officer on the northern expedition board of the Prince of Baling, and as a penal officer on the pacification army board of the Prince of Ancheng; when that establishment became the Chariots and Cavalry staff, he transferred with it.
value.literal: Yan, at the end of the Song era of Daming, first entered service as a regular attendant in the princedom of Linhe, then as an outside-section gentleman, as a staff officer on the northern expedition board of the Prince of Baling, as a penal officer on the pacification army board of the Prince of Ancheng, and followed the establishment when it became the Chariots and Cavalry staff.

value.zh: 晉熙王燮爲郢州，晏爲安西主簿。
value.en: When Prince Xie of Jinxing was assigned to Ying Province, Yan served as his western pacification chief clerk.
value.literal: When the Prince of Jinxing, Xie, was made governor of Ying Province, Yan was his western pacification chief clerk.

value.zh: 世祖爲長史，與晏相遇。
value.en: The future Emperor Wudi of Qi was chief administrator there, and he and Yan became acquainted.
value.literal: The Heir Apparent was chief administrator, and met Yan.

value.zh: 府轉鎮西，板晏記室諮議。
value.en: When the establishment was reorganized as the western pacification staff, Yan was appointed recorder and adviser on its board.
value.literal: When the establishment became western pacification, Yan was appointed on its board as recorder and adviser.

value.zh: 沈攸之事難，鎮西職僚皆隨世祖鎮盆城，上時權勢雖重，而衆情猶有疑惑，晏便專心奉事，軍旅書翰皆委焉。
value.en: During the crisis of Shen Youzhi's rebellion, the western pacification staff followed the Heir Apparent to garrison Pencheng. Though his power was already formidable, many still hesitated; Yan devoted himself wholeheartedly to his service, and all military correspondence was placed in his hands.
value.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair brought crisis, the western pacification staff all followed the Heir Apparent to garrison Pencheng; though his power was already weighty, popular sentiment still harbored doubts, and Yan then devoted himself to service—military and documentary matters were all entrusted to him.

value.zh: 性甚便僻，漸見親侍。
value.en: He was clever and obliging by nature, and gradually won intimate favor.
value.literal: His nature was very adaptable and accommodating, and he gradually came to be treated with intimate attendance.

value.zh: 乃留爲上征虜撫軍府板諮議，領記室。
value.en: He was then kept on as a board adviser on the Heir Apparent's Campaigning-Caitiffs and Pacification Army staff, concurrently heading the Record Office.
value.literal: He was then retained as a board adviser of the Heir Apparent's northern expedition and pacification army staff, concurrently heading the recorder's office.

value.zh: 從還都，遷領軍司馬，中軍從事中郎。
value.en: On their return to the capital, he was promoted to marshal of the Palace Guard and attendant gentleman of the central army.
value.literal: When they returned to the capital, he was transferred to be marshal of the Palace Guard, and an attendant gentleman of the central army.

value.zh: 常在上府，參議機密。
value.en: He was constantly at the Heir Apparent's establishment, participating in confidential deliberations.
value.literal: He was constantly at the Heir Apparent's establishment, taking part in confidential deliberation.

value.zh: 建元初，轉太子中庶子。
value.en: At the beginning of the Jianyuan era, he was transferred to junior mentor of the heir apparent.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyuan era, he was transferred to be a junior mentor of the heir apparent.

value.zh: 世祖在東宮，專斷朝事，多不聞啓，晏慮及罪，稱疾自疏。
value.en: While the Heir Apparent held court from the Eastern Palace, he often decided state affairs on his own without reporting them upward. Yan feared he would be held accountable and pleaded illness to keep his distance.
value.literal: The Heir Apparent in the Eastern Palace made sole decisions on court affairs and often did not report them; Yan feared he would be implicated in guilt and claimed illness to distance himself.

value.zh: 尋領射聲校尉，不拜。
value.en: He was soon appointed colonel of the Archers' Guard but declined to take up the post.
value.literal: Soon he was made to head the Archers' Guard, but he did not accept the appointment.

value.zh: 世祖卽位，轉長兼侍中，意任如舊。
value.en: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Yan was transferred to acting Attendant-in-Ordinary, with the same trust and favor as before.
value.literal: When the Heir Apparent took the throne, Yan was transferred to acting regular attendant-in-ordinary, with trust and appointment as before.

value.zh: 永明元年，領步兵校尉，遷侍中祭酒，校尉如故。
value.en: In the first year of Yongming, he was made colonel of the Footsoldiers Guard and promoted to attendant-in-ordinary and libationer, retaining his colonelcy.
value.literal: In the first year of Yongming, he headed the Footsoldiers Guard, was promoted to attendant-in-ordinary and libationer, and retained his colonelcy.

value.zh: 遭母喪，起爲輔國將軍、司徒左長史。
value.en: After his mother's death, he was recalled from mourning to serve as General Who Assists the State and left chief administrator of the Minister of Education.
value.literal: When his mother died, he was recalled from mourning to be a general who assists the state and left chief administrator of the Minister of Education.

value.zh: 晏父普曜藉晏勢宦，多歷通官。
value.en: Yan's father Wang Puyao, relying on his son's influence, held a succession of high offices.
value.literal: Yan's father Puyao, relying on Yan's power in office, passed through many high offices.

value.zh: 晏尋遷左衞將軍，加給事中。
value.en: Yan was soon made General of the Left Guard with the additional title of supervisor of attendance.
value.literal: Yan was soon transferred to be General of the Left Guard and was given the additional title of supervisor of attendance.

value.zh: 未拜，而普曜卒，居喪有稱。
value.en: Before he could take up the post, Puyao died; Yan's conduct in mourning won praise.
value.literal: Before he took up the appointment, Puyao died; in mourning he won praise.

value.zh: 起冠軍將軍、司徒左長史、濟陽太守，未拜，遷衞尉，將軍如故。
value.en: He was recalled from mourning as Champion General, left chief administrator of the Minister of Education, and Administrator of Jiyang; before accepting those posts he was transferred to Commandant of the Guard, retaining his general's rank.
value.literal: He was recalled as Champion General, left chief administrator of the Minister of Education, and Administrator of Jiyang; before he took up the posts he was transferred to be Commandant of the Guard, retaining his generalship.

value.zh: 四年，轉太子詹事，加散騎常侍。
value.en: In the fourth year, he was made steward of the heir apparent's household with the additional title of irregular attendant-in-ordinary.
value.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to be steward of the heir apparent's household, with the additional title of irregular attendant-in-ordinary.

value.zh: 六年，轉丹陽尹，常侍如故。
value.en: In the sixth year, he was made intendant of Danyang, retaining his title as irregular attendant-in-ordinary.
value.literal: In the sixth year, he was transferred to be intendant of Danyang, retaining his irregular attendant title.

value.zh: 晏位任親重，朝夕進見，言論朝事，自豫章王嶷、尚書令王儉皆降意以接之，而晏每以疏漏被上呵責，連稱疾久之。
value.en: Yan held an intimate and weighty position, seeing the emperor morning and evening and discussing state affairs. Even the Prince of Yuzhang, Xie, and the Director of the Department of State Affairs, Wang Jian, treated him with deference—yet Yan was often rebuked for careless mistakes and repeatedly pleaded illness for extended periods.
value.literal: Yan's position and appointment were intimate and weighty; morning and evening he was received in audience and discussed court affairs. From the Prince of Yuzhang, Xie, to the Director of the Department of State Affairs, Wang Jian, all lowered their manner to receive him—but Yan was often rebuked by the emperor for oversights and repeatedly claimed illness for long periods.

value.zh: 上以晏須祿養，七年，轉爲江州刺史，晏固辭不願出外，見許，留爲吏部尚書，領太子右衞率。
value.en: The emperor felt Yan needed an income to support himself, so in the seventh year he was appointed governor of Jiang Province. Yan firmly declined to leave the capital; the emperor agreed and kept him on as Director of the Ministry of Personnel, concurrently heading the heir apparent's right guard.
value.literal: Because the emperor thought Yan needed salary to support himself, in the seventh year he was transferred to be governor of Jiang Province; Yan firmly declined and did not wish to go outside the capital. Permission was granted, and he was retained as Director of the Ministry of Personnel, concurrently heading the heir apparent's right guard.

value.zh: 終以舊恩見寵。
value.en: He continued to enjoy favor on account of their long-standing bond.
value.literal: In the end he was favored because of old kindness.

value.zh: 時尚書令王儉雖貴而疏，晏旣領選，權行臺閣，與儉頗不平。
value.en: At the time Director Wang Jian, though eminent, stood somewhat apart from the emperor; once Yan took charge of personnel selection, he exercised secretariat power and clashed with Jian.
value.literal: At the time the Director Wang Jian, though eminent, was distant; once Yan headed selection, he exercised power in the secretariat and was rather at odds with Jian.

value.zh: 儉卒，禮官議諡，上欲依王導諡爲「文獻」，晏啓上曰：「導乃得此諡，但宋以來，不加素族。」
value.en: When Jian died, the ritual officers debated his posthumous title. The emperor wished to follow Wang Dao's example and grant the title "Literary and Presented." Yan memorialized the throne: "Only Dao deserved that title—and since the Song, plain families have not received it."
value.literal: When Jian died, the ritual officers debated his posthumous title; the emperor wished to follow Wang Dao and give the title "Literary and Presented," and Yan memorialized the throne, saying: "Dao alone could receive this title, but since the Song, plain families have not been given it."

value.zh: 出謂親人曰：「平頭憲事已行矣。」
value.en: Leaving the audience, he told his intimates, "That business with flat-top Xian is settled."
value.literal: Going out, he said to his intimates: "The affair of the flat-topped Xian is already done."

value.zh: 八年，改領右衞將軍，陳疾自解。
value.en: In the eighth year he was made to head the Right Guard, then pleaded illness and resigned.
value.literal: In the eighth year, he was changed to head the Right Guard, and pleaded illness to resign.

value.zh: 上欲以高宗代晏領選，手敕問之。
value.en: The emperor wished to have Xiao Luan replace Yan in charge of selection and sent a handwritten edict to ask Yan's opinion.
value.literal: The emperor wished to have Gaozong replace Yan in heading selection, and sent a handwritten edict to ask him.

value.zh: 晏啓曰：「鸞清幹有餘，然不諳百氏，恐不可居此職。」
value.en: Yan replied, "Luan is certainly capable and upright, but he is not versed in the great families—I fear he cannot hold this post."
value.literal: Yan memorialized: "Luan has more than enough purity and capacity, yet he is not versed in the hundred clans—I fear he cannot hold this office."

value.zh: 上乃止。
value.en: The emperor dropped the plan.
value.literal: The emperor then stopped.

value.zh: 明年，遷侍中，領太子詹事，本州中正，又以疾辭。
value.en: The following year he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household and Rectifier of his home province, but again resigned citing illness.
value.literal: The next year he was transferred to attendant-in-ordinary, heading the heir apparent's household and serving as chief assessor of his native province, and again resigned on grounds of illness.

value.zh: 十年，改授散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，給親信二十人，中正如故。
value.en: In the tenth year he was reassigned as irregular attendant-in-ordinary and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, given twenty trusted attendants, and retained his assessor title.
value.literal: In the tenth year he was reassigned as irregular attendant-in-ordinary and as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, given twenty trusted attendants, and retained his assessor title.

value.zh: 十一年，遷右僕射，領太孫右衞率。
value.en: In the eleventh year he was made right vice director, concurrently heading the crown prince's right guard.
value.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to be right vice director, concurrently heading the heir apparent of the heir apparent's right guard.

value.zh: 世祖崩，遺旨以尚書事付晏及徐孝嗣，令久於其職。
value.en: When Emperor Wudi died, his testament entrusted Department of State Affairs affairs to Yan and Xu Xiaosi, instructing them to hold their posts for the long term.
value.literal: When the emperor died, his testamentary instruction entrusted Department of State Affairs affairs to Yan and Xu Xiaosi, ordering them to hold their offices long.

value.zh: 鬱林卽位，轉左僕射，中正如故。
value.en: When Emperor Yulin ascended the throne, Yan was made left vice director, retaining his assessor title.
value.literal: When Yulin took the throne, Yan was transferred to left vice director, retaining his assessor title.

value.zh: 隆昌元年，加侍中。
value.en: In the first year of Longchang he was given the additional title of attendant-in-ordinary.
value.literal: In the first year of Longchang, he was given the additional title of attendant-in-ordinary.

value.zh: 高宗謀廢立，晏便響應推奉。
value.en: When Xiao Luan plotted to depose the emperor and enthrone himself, Yan immediately supported the move.
value.literal: When Gaozong plotted deposition and enthronement, Yan at once responded and promoted his elevation.

value.zh: 延興元年，轉尚書令，加後將軍，侍中、中正如故。
value.en: In the first year of Yanxing he was made Director of the Department of State Affairs with the additional title of rear general, retaining his titles as attendant-in-ordinary and chief assessor.
value.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, he was transferred to Director of the Department of State Affairs, with the additional title of rear general; his attendant and assessor titles remained.

value.zh: 封曲江縣侯，邑千戶。
value.en: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qujiang with a fief of one thousand households.
value.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qujiang County, with a fief of a thousand households.

value.zh: 給鼓吹一部，甲仗五十人入殿。
value.en: He was granted a full set of martial music and fifty armed retainers permitted to enter the palace halls.
value.literal: He was given one set of martial music and fifty armed men allowed to enter the palace hall.

value.zh: 高宗與晏宴於東府，語及時事，晏扺掌曰：「公常言晏怯，今定何如？」
value.en: At a feast in the Eastern Establishment, Gaozong and Yan discussed current affairs. Yan clapped his hands and said, "Your Grace always called me timid—what do you think now?"
value.literal: Gaozong feasted with Yan at the Eastern Establishment and spoke of current affairs; Yan clapped his hands and said: "Your Grace always said Yan was timid—how about now?"

value.zh: 建武元年，進號驃騎大將軍，給班劔二十人，侍中、令、中正如故。
value.en: In the first year of Jianwu his title was advanced to Rapid Cavalry General-in-Chief; he was given twenty ceremonial guards with blades and retained his titles as attendant-in-ordinary, director, and chief assessor.
value.literal: In the first year of Jianwu, his title was advanced to Rapid Cavalry General-in-Chief; he was given twenty ceremonial guards with blades, and retained his attendant, director, and assessor titles.

value.zh: 又加兵百人，領太子少傅，進爵爲公，增邑爲二千戶。
value.en: He was further given a hundred troops, appointed junior mentor of the heir apparent, advanced to duke, and his fief increased to two thousand households.
value.literal: He was further given a hundred troops, made to head the heir apparent's junior mentor, advanced in rank to duke, and his fief increased to two thousand households.

value.zh: 以虜動，給兵千人。
value.en: Because of northern incursions, he was given an additional thousand troops.
value.literal: Because the barbarians were active, he was given a thousand troops.

value.zh: 晏爲人篤於親舊，爲世祖所稱。
value.en: Yan was devoted to kin and old friends, a quality the late emperor had praised.
value.literal: Yan as a man was devoted to kin and old friends, and was praised by the late emperor.

value.zh: 至是自謂佐命惟新，言論常非薄世祖故事，衆始怪之。
value.en: From then on he regarded himself as a founder of the new regime and often spoke slightingly of the late emperor's ways, to the astonishment of many.
value.literal: From this point he considered himself a founder of the new order; in speech he often disparaged the late emperor's ways, and people first found it strange.

value.zh: 高宗雖以事際須晏，而心相疑斥，料簡世祖中詔，得與晏手敕三百餘紙，皆是論國家事，以此愈猜薄之。
value.en: Though Gaozong still needed Yan for the moment, he distrusted him inwardly. Reviewing the late emperor's confidential edicts, he found more than three hundred handwritten orders to Yan on state affairs, which only deepened his suspicion and coldness toward him.
value.literal: Although Gaozong needed Yan because of the circumstances, in his heart he suspected and rejected him; sorting through the late emperor's confidential edicts, he found more than three hundred sheets of handwritten orders to Yan, all discussing state affairs—by this he grew still more suspicious and cold toward him.

value.zh: 初卽位，始安王遙光便勸誅晏，帝曰：「晏於我有勳，且未有罪。」
value.en: Soon after his accession, Prince Yaoguang of Shian urged that Yan be executed. The emperor said, "Yan has served me well, and he has committed no crime."
value.literal: When he first took the throne, the Prince of Shian, Yaoguang, at once urged executing Yan; the emperor said: "Yan has merit toward me, and as yet has no crime."

value.zh: 遙光曰：「晏尚不能爲武帝，安能爲陛下。」
value.en: Yaoguang replied, "If he could not even be loyal to Emperor Wu, how can he be loyal to you?"
value.literal: Yaoguang said: "If Yan could not even serve Emperor Wu, how can he serve Your Majesty?"

value.zh: 帝默然變色。
value.en: The emperor fell silent, his expression darkening.
value.literal: The emperor fell silent and changed color.

value.zh: 時帝常遣心腹左右陳世範等出塗巷採聽異言，由是以晏爲事。
value.en: The emperor often sent trusted attendants such as Chen Shifan into the streets to listen for rumors, and through them Yan became the focus of suspicion.
value.literal: At the time the emperor often sent trusted personal attendants such as Chen Shifan into the lanes to gather and listen for unusual talk; by this they made Yan their target.

value.zh: 晏輕淺無防慮，望開府，數呼相工自視，云當大貴。
value.en: Yan was careless and indiscreet. Hoping for appointment as grand minister, he repeatedly summoned fortune-tellers to read his features and declared that he was destined for great rank.
value.literal: Yan was frivolous and without precaution; he hoped for an establishment as a grand minister, repeatedly summoned physiognomists to examine himself, and said he would attain great eminence.

value.zh: 與賔客語，好屏人清間，上聞之，疑晏欲反，遂有誅晏之意。
value.en: When talking with guests he liked to dismiss attendants for private conversation. When the emperor heard of this, he suspected Yan of plotting rebellion and resolved to kill him.
value.literal: When speaking with guests he liked to dismiss others for a quiet private talk; when the emperor heard of it, he suspected Yan intended rebellion and thus formed the intention to execute him.

value.zh: 傖人鮮于文粲與晏子德元往來，密探朝旨，告晏有異志。
value.en: The northern subject Xianyu Wencan associated with Yan's son Deyuan, secretly probed court intentions, and reported that Yan harbored treasonous designs.
value.literal: The barbarian-subject Xianyu Wencan had dealings with Yan's son Deyuan, secretly probed court intentions, and reported that Yan harbored a different will.

value.zh: 世範等又啓上云：「晏謀因四年南郊，與世祖故舊主帥於道中竊發。」
value.en: Shifan and others further reported, "Yan plans to use the southern suburban sacrifice in the fourth year to launch a surprise attack on the road with the late emperor's old commanders."
value.literal: Shifan and others further memorialized the throne: "Yan plots, taking advantage of the southern suburban sacrifice in the fourth year, to launch a surprise attack on the road with the late emperor's old commanders."

value.zh: 會虎犯郊壇，帝愈懼。
value.en: When a tiger appeared at the suburban altar, the emperor grew still more alarmed.
value.literal: It happened that a tiger invaded the suburban altar, and the emperor grew still more fearful.

value.zh: 未郊一日，敕停行。
value.en: One day before the sacrifice, an edict canceled the ceremony.
value.literal: One day before the sacrifice, an edict halted the ceremony.

value.zh: 元會畢，乃召晏於華林省誅之。
value.en: After the New Year's audience concluded, he summoned Yan to the Hualin Pavilion and had him executed.
value.literal: When the New Year's audience was finished, he summoned Yan to the Hualin Pavilion and executed him.

value.zh: 下詔曰：「晏閭閻凡伍，少無持操，階緣人乏，班齒官途。
value.en: An edict was issued: "Yan came from common stock, showed no firm character in youth, and climbed the official ladder by exploiting others' weaknesses.
value.literal: An edict was issued: "Yan was of common lanes and ordinary ranks, in youth without settled conduct; he climbed by others' want and took his place on the official ladder.

value.zh: 世祖在蕃，搜揚擢用，弃略疵瑕，遂升要重。
value.en: While still a prince, the late emperor sought him out and promoted him, overlooking his faults, until he rose to the highest offices.
value.literal: When the late emperor was in his princedom, he sought and promoted him, overlooking flaws and blemishes, and thus raised him to crucial weight.

value.zh: 而輕跳險銳，在貴彌著，猜忌反覆，觸情多端。
value.en: Yet he was frivolous, rash, and treacherous; the higher he rose, the worse these traits became—suspicious, changeable, and driven by whim.
value.literal: Yet he was frivolous, rash, dangerous, and sharp; the higher his rank, the more evident it became—suspicious, changeable, and touching feelings in many ways.

value.zh: 故以兩宮所弗容，十手所共指。
value.en: For this reason neither palace could tolerate him, and all pointed him out as a danger.
value.literal: Therefore both palaces could not tolerate him, and ten hands pointed at him together.

value.zh: 旣內愧于心，外懼憲牘，掩迹陳痾，多歷年載。
value.en: Feeling guilty within and fearing prosecution without, he hid himself behind repeated claims of illness for many years.
value.literal: Having inward shame in his heart and outward fear of the law's documents, he concealed his tracks and claimed illness for many years.

value.zh: 頻授蕃任，輙辭請不行，事似謙虛，情實詭伏。
value.en: Repeatedly offered provincial posts, he always declined to leave the capital—an appearance of modesty that masked deceit.
value.literal: Repeatedly given provincial appointments, he always declined and would not go—outwardly seeming modest, inwardly truly deceitful and hidden.

value.zh: 隆昌以來，運集艱難，匡贊之功，頗有心力。
value.en: Since the Longchang era, when the dynasty faced grave trials, he had contributed real effort to restoring order.
value.literal: Since Longchang, when fortune gathered in hardship, his merit in supporting and assisting showed considerable effort of heart.

value.zh: 迺爵冠通侯，位登元輔，綢繆恩寄，朝莫均焉。
value.en: He was then ennobled as a full marquis, raised to chief minister, and showered with favor morning and evening alike.
value.literal: Then his noble rank crowned full marquisates, his office reached chief minister, and intimate favor bound him morning and evening alike.

value.zh: 谿壑可盈，無厭將及。
value.en: Yet ravines may be filled, but his greed knew no limit.
value.literal: Ravines and gullies can be filled—his lack of satiety was about to reach its limit.

value.zh: 視天畫地，遂懷異圖。
value.en: He looked to heaven and plotted on earth, harboring treasonous designs.
value.literal: Looking to heaven and tracing on earth, he then harbored a different design.

value.zh: 廣求卜相，取信巫覡。
value.en: He sought out diviners and fortune-tellers and put his faith in shamans.
value.literal: He widely sought divination and physiognomy and put faith in shamans.

value.zh: 論薦黨附，徧滿臺府。
value.en: He packed the secretariat with his own faction through recommendations and patronage.
value.literal: He discussed recommendations and formed factions until they filled the secretariat.

value.zh: 令大息德元淵藪亡命，同惡相濟，劔客成羣。
value.en: His eldest son Deyuan harbored fugitives and outlaws; villains aided one another until swordsmen gathered in gangs.
value.literal: He had his eldest son Deyuan harbor fugitives in deep lairs; evildoers aided one another and swordsmen formed gangs.

value.zh: 弟詡凶愚，遠相脣齒，信驛往來，密通要契。
value.en: His younger brother Xu was brutal and foolish; though far apart, they acted as mutual allies, exchanging couriers and secret agreements.
value.literal: His younger brother Xu was fierce and foolish; from afar they were lip and teeth to each other, with couriers going back and forth and secret communications of crucial pacts.

value.zh: 去歲之初，奉朝請鮮于文粲備告姦謀。
value.en: Early last year the court gentleman Xianyu Wencan reported the full details of the conspiracy.
value.literal: At the beginning of last year, the court gentleman Xianyu Wencan fully reported the treacherous plot.

value.zh: 朕以信必由中，義無與貳，推誠委任，覬能悛改。
value.en: Believing that trust must come from the heart and that loyalty admits no division, We extended Our trust to him, hoping he would reform.
value.literal: We, believing trust must come from within and that in righteousness there is no divided loyalty, extended sincerity and entrusted him, hoping he could reform.

value.zh: 而長惡易流，構扇彌大，與北中郎司馬蕭毅、臺隊主劉明達等剋期竊發。
value.en: Instead he clung to evil and spread unrest ever wider, setting a date for a surprise rising with the northern central army's staff officer Xiao Yi, the palace guard commander Liu Mingda, and others.
value.literal: Yet he long cherished evil and easily spread it; his agitation grew ever greater, and with the northern central army's staff officer Xiao Yi, the palace guard commander Liu Mingda, and others he set a date for a surprise rising.

value.zh: 以河東王鉉識用微弱，可爲其主，得志之日，當守以虛器。
value.en: They intended to make Prince Xuan of Hedong, whose abilities were slight, their puppet ruler, keeping him as a figurehead once they seized power.
value.literal: Taking the Prince of Hedong, Xuan, whose knowledge and capacity were weak, as one who could serve as their lord—on the day they succeeded, he would be kept as an empty vessel.

value.zh: 明達諸辭列，炳然具存。
value.en: Mingda's confessions and lists of accomplices remain fully on record.
value.literal: Mingda's various statements and lists are clear and fully preserved.

value.zh: 昔漢后以反脣致討，魏臣以虯鬚爲戮，況無君之心旣彰，陵上之迹斯著，此而可容，誰寘刑辟。
value.en: In former times the Han empress was punished for insolent speech and a Wei minister was executed for his arrogance—how much more when disloyalty is plain and the crime of lèse-majesté is evident? If this can be tolerated, who would ever face the law?
value.literal: Formerly the Han empress was punished for turning her lip against authority, and a Wei minister was executed for his curling beard—how much more when a heart without a ruler is already manifest and traces of climbing above one's lord are thus clear: if this can be tolerated, who would be placed within the penal code?

value.zh: 竝可收付廷尉，肅明國典。」
value.en: Let all of them be handed over to the Minister of Justice so that the law may be enforced."
value.literal: All may be taken and delivered to the Minister of Justice to clarify the state's statutes."

value.zh: 晏未敗數日，於北山廟答賽，夜還，晏旣醉，部伍人亦飲酒，羽儀錯亂，前後十餘里中，不復相禁制，識者云「此勢不復久也」。
value.en: Several days before his downfall, Yan offered thanks at the Beishan temple. Returning at night drunk, with his escort also drinking, his ceremonial guard fell into disorder for more than ten li in every direction. Observers said, "Such power cannot last."
value.literal: Several days before Yan's fall, he made a thanksgiving offering at the Beishan temple; returning at night, Yan was already drunk, and his escort men also drank wine—the ceremonial guard fell into disorder, and for more than ten li before and behind, restraint was no longer kept. Observers said, "This power will not last long."

value.zh: 晏子德元，有意尚。
value.en: Yan's son Deyuan had ability and refinement.
value.literal: Yan's son Deyuan had aspiration and refinement.

value.zh: 至車騎長史。
value.en: He rose to chief administrator of the Chariots and Cavalry staff.
value.literal: He reached the post of chief administrator of the Chariots and Cavalry staff.

value.zh: 德元初名湛，世祖謂晏曰：「劉湛、江湛，竝不善終，此非佳名也。」
value.en: Deyuan's original name was Zhan. The late emperor told Yan, "Liu Zhan and Jiang Zhan both came to bad ends—this is not an auspicious name."
value.literal: Deyuan's original name was Zhan; the late emperor said to Yan: "Liu Zhan and Jiang Zhan both did not end well—this is not a fine name."

value.zh: 晏乃改之。
value.en: Yan then changed his son's name.
value.literal: Yan then changed it.

value.zh: 至是與弟晉安王友德和俱被誅。
value.en: At this time he and his younger brother Dehe, a friend of the Prince of Jin'an, were both executed.
value.literal: At this time he and his younger brother, the Prince of Jin'an's friend Dehe, were both executed.

value.zh: 晏弟詡，永明中爲少府卿。
value.en: Yan's younger brother Xu served as Minister of the Privy Purse during the Yongming era.
value.literal: Yan's younger brother Xu, in the Yongming era, was Minister of the Privy Purse.

value.zh: 六年，敕位未登黃門郎，不得畜女妓。
value.en: In the sixth year an edict declared that officials below the rank of Yellow Gate Gentleman might not keep female entertainers.
value.literal: In the sixth year, an edict ordered that those whose rank had not reached Yellow Gate Gentleman might not keep female entertainers.

value.zh: 詡與射聲校尉陰玄智坐畜妓免官，禁錮十年。
value.en: Xu and Colonel Yin Xuanzhi of the Archers' Guard were dismissed for keeping entertainers and confined for ten years.
value.literal: Xu and the Archers' Guard colonel Yin Xuanzhi were dismissed from office for keeping entertainers and confined for ten years.

value.zh: 敕特原詡禁錮。
value.en: An edict specially remitted Xu's confinement.
value.literal: An edict specially remitted Xu's confinement.

value.zh: 後出爲輔國將軍、始興內史。
value.en: He was later appointed General Who Assists the State and interior minister of Shixing.
value.literal: Later he went out as General Who Assists the State and interior minister of Shixing.

value.zh: 廣州刺史劉纘爲奴所殺，詡率郡兵討之。
value.en: When Administrator Liu Zuan of Guang Province was killed by a slave, Xu led commandery troops to punish the killers.
value.literal: The Administrator of Guang Province, Liu Zuan, was killed by a slave; Xu led commandery troops to punish them.

value.zh: 延興元年，授詡持節廣州刺史。
value.en: In the first year of Yanxing, Xu was appointed Administrator of Guang Province with credentials bearing the imperial staff.
value.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, Xu was given the staff of authority as Administrator of Guang Province.

value.zh: 詡亦篤舊。
value.en: Xu, too, was devoted to old friends and kin.
value.literal: Xu, too, was devoted to old ties.

value.zh: 晏誅，上又遣南中郎司馬蕭季敞襲詡殺之。
